q: The SI unit of force is?
exp: The SI unit of force is the Newton (N). Answer: Newton

q: Light travels fastest through which medium?
exp: Light has maximum speed (3×10⁸ m/s) in vacuum. Answer: Vacuum

q: Which law states that for every action there is an equal and opposite reaction?
exp: Newton's Third Law of Motion states: every action has an equal and opposite reaction. Answer: Newton's Third Law

q: The boiling point of water at sea level in Celsius scale is?
exp: Water boils at 100°C at standard atmospheric pressure. Answer: 100°C

q: Sound cannot travel through which of the following?
exp: Sound is a mechanical wave and requires a medium; it cannot travel through vacuum. Answer: Vacuum

q: The SI unit of electric current is?
exp: The SI unit of electric current is the Ampere (A). Answer: Ampere

q: A concave mirror is used in which of the following?
exp: Concave mirrors form magnified erect images (when object is within focal length), used as shaving/makeup mirrors. Answer: Shaving mirror

q: The phenomenon of splitting of white light into seven colours by a prism is called?
exp: Dispersion is the splitting of white light into its constituent colours (VIBGYOR) by a prism. Answer: Dispersion

q: Which of the following is a vector quantity?
exp: Displacement has both magnitude and direction, so it is a vector quantity. Answer: Displacement

q: The escape velocity from Earth's surface is approximately?
exp: The escape velocity from Earth is about 11.2 km/s. Answer: 11.2 km/s
Ohm's Law: V = IR (voltage = current × resistance). Answer: Voltage, current and resistance

q: The splitting of a heavy nucleus into two lighter nuclei is called?
exp: Nuclear fission is the splitting of a heavy nucleus (e.g., uranium) into lighter nuclei. Answer: Nuclear fission

q: The blue colour of the sky is due to which phenomenon?
exp: The sky appears blue because shorter blue wavelengths are scattered more by air molecules (Rayleigh scattering). Answer: Scattering of light (Rayleigh scattering)

q: Which physical quantity is measured in 'Candela'?
exp: Candela (cd) is the SI unit of luminous intensity. Answer: Luminous intensity

q: The working principle of a nuclear reactor is based on which reaction?
exp: Nuclear reactors use controlled nuclear fission chain reactions (e.g., of uranium-235). Answer: Nuclear fission chain reaction
